newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Irish bonds trading at top end of narrow ranges.
newsitem.headline: Irish bonds trading at top end of narrow ranges.

text.p: Irish government bonds were trading at the top end of thin ranges in late trade on Thursday as the market awaited the release of end-December banking statistics by the Central Bank at 1630 GMT, dealers said.
"What we've seen on the day is further buying in the 10-year area especially, although the five-year area is also well supported," one dealer said.
"Domestically we are awaiting the release of the Central Bank numbers while Friday sees the release of non-farm payrolls data in the U.S.," the dealer added.
Economists' forecasts range from 15 to 17 percent for Irish credit growth in the month of December compared with 16.4 percent at end-November.
U.S. January payrolls data and jobless claims are scheduled for release at 1330 GMT on Friday.

By 1610 GMT, the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 was up 15 pence from Wednesday's close at 110.17 to yield 6.52 percent while the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 had gained 20 pence from the close to 102.75 to yield 5.81 percent.
Dealers said Irish bonds were trading at 89 basis points over German bunds in the 10-year area and 144 basis points over bunds in the five-year area.
